This Advice message is being issued for Coomboona, Mooroopna North.
  • A large pile of industrial waste is on fire near Coomboona Road, Coomboona.    
  • The fire is now under control. 
  • Emergency services have left the scene and are monitoring the situation. 
  • This Advice replaces the warning issued at 08.45AM, Sunday 09 August 2026. 
There is currently no threat to the community, but you should continue to stay informed and monitor conditions.
What you should do:
  • If you are sensitive to smoke or you live with someone who is sensitive to smoke, you should close windows and doors. Turn off heating and cooling systems. 
  • To prevent the smell of smoke entering your home or business, close windows and doors.  
Impacts in your area:
  • Smoke will be visible from nearby roads and communities. 

This message was issued by Country Fire Authority.

The next update is expected by 10/08/2026 12:10 pm or as the situation changes.

properties.webBody:
This Moderate Flood Warning is being issued for the King River.

MODERATE FLOODING POSSIBLE AT DOCKER ROAD BRIDGE MONDAY MORNING AND A MODERATE FLOOD PEAK IS LIKELY AT GRETA SOUTH MONDAY MORNING

MINOR FLOODING OCCURRING DOWNSTREAM OF LAKE WILLIAM HOVELL AND LIKELY AT BRIGHT,EUROBIN AND ROCKY POINT FROM MONDAY MORNING

MINOR FLOODING POSSIBLE AT WANGARATTA FROM MONDAY EVENING AND DOWNSTREAM OFLAKE BUFFALO FROM MONDAY AFTERNOON

Rainfall across the Ovens and King River catchment since Sunday morning has resulted river level rises and minor flooding along the Ovens and King Rivers. Rainfall is forecast to continue until Monday afternoon, which may result in further river level rises and areas of minor to moderate flooding. 

The situation is being closely monitored, and this warning will be updated as required. 

A Flood Watch is current for parts of North East, Gippsland and Central Victoria.

King River
Moderate flooding is possible at Docker Road Bridge. Minor flooding is occurring at Lake William Hovell (Downstream) and Cheshunt. The King River at Lake William Hovell (Downstream) is currently at 1.83 m and rising, with minor flooding.

The King River at Lake William Hovell (Downstream) may remain above the minor flood level (1.80 m) during Monday. 

Further rises are possible with forecast rain.No observations are currently available for the King River at Docker Rd Bridge. The river level is estimated tobe below the minor flood level. 

The King River at Docker Rd Bridge is likely to exceed the minor flood level(3.70 m) early Monday morning. The river may exceed the moderate flood level (3.95 m) Monday morning. 

Further rises are possible.
Stay safe - avoid the flooded area. Be aware of potential hazards caused by flooding and never enter floodwater.
What you should do:
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never enter floodwater.
If you choose to leave:
  • Remember to take your pets, mobile phone, spare clothes and medications.
  • Travel to the home of family or friends who are in a safe location, away from flooding.
  • Turn off gas and electricity at your home or workplace.
  • Be aware of any road closures when you leave.
If you are travelling:
  • Do not enter flooded areas. Turn around a find a safe alternative route.
  • Be aware of road hazards including mud, debris and damaged roads or bridges.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
If you stay or if it is unsafe to leave:
  • Make sure you have enough food, drinking water, medications and pet food to survive for three to five days in case you become isolated.
  • Use plugs, sandbags or household items to block toilets, sinks and drains to stop sewerage backflow.
  • Lift it - move valuables and vital household items up on high surfaces, such as on top of tables, chairs, benches and beds.

Impacts in your area:

Impacts in your area:
  • Flooding above floor level of a single-story home is likely to occur in some locations.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 10/08/2026 12:00 pm or as the situation changes.

This Moderate Flood Warning is being issued for the Seven Creeks to Euroa.

MODERATE FLOODING OCCURRING AT STRATHBOGIE AND POSSIBLE AT EUROA FROM MONDAY MORNING.

Rainfall across the Seven and Castle Creeks catchments since Sunday morning has resulted creek level rises and minor to moderate flooding. Rainfall is forecast to continue until Monday afternoon, which may result in further creek level rises and areas of flooding across the Seven and Castle Creeks catchments.

The situation is being closely monitored, and this warning will be updated as required.

Seven Creeks to Euroa
Moderate flooding is occurring along the Seven Creeks at Strathbogie and is possible at Euroa. The Seven Creeks at Euroa is currently at 2.81 m and rising, with minor flooding. 

The Seven Creeks at Euroa may exceed the moderate flood level (4.00 m) Monday morning.

Stay safe - avoid the flooded area. Be aware of potential hazards caused by flooding and never enter floodwater.
What you should do:
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never enter floodwater.
If you choose to leave:
  • Remember to take your pets, mobile phone, spare clothes and medications.
  • Travel to the home of family or friends who are in a safe location, away from flooding.
  • Turn off gas and electricity at your home or workplace.
  • Be aware of any road closures when you leave.
If you are travelling:
  • Do not enter flooded areas. Turn around a find a safe alternative route.
  • Be aware of road hazards including mud, debris and damaged roads or bridges.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
If you stay or if it is unsafe to leave:
  • Make sure you have enough food, drinking water, medications and pet food to survive for three to five days in case you become isolated.
  • Use plugs, sandbags or household items to block toilets, sinks and drains to stop sewerage backflow.
  • Lift it - move valuables and vital household items up on high surfaces, such as on top of tables, chairs, benches and beds.

Impacts in your area:

Impacts in your area:
  • Flooding above floor level of a single-story home is likely to occur in some locations.

At a river height of 2.5m (Minor Flood Level)
  • Stormwater drains compromised in town due to water level in creek.

This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for the Broken River to Benalla.

Minor flooding possible at Benalla from Monday Morning.

Rainfall across the Broken River catchments since Sunday morning has resulted river level rises. Rainfall is forecast to continue until Monday afternoon, which may result in further river level rises and areas of floodingalong the Broken River. 

The situation is being closely monitored, and this warning will be updated as required.

A Flood Watch is current for parts of North East, Gippsland and Central Victoria.

Broken River to Benalla

Minor flooding may occur along the Broken River to Benalla.

The Broken River at Benalla is currently at 1.83 m and rising, below the minor flood level. The Broken Rive rat Benalla may exceed the minor flood level (2.50 m) Monday morning. 

Further rises are possible. 

Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
